result.title: When Agent Skills Go Stale: Runtime Behavior and Selective Maintenance in Evolving Environments
result.summary: Agent skills use past experience and current observations to guide decisions and actions on related tasks. This experience is retained in skill state, whose reuse can amortize inference-time reasoning and environment interaction. When environment changes, parts of this state can become outdated while others remain useful. Across four task settings and two models, we compare skill reuse before and after environment changes. Previously beneficial skills can reduce task performance by over 10 percentage points or increase execution cost by nearly 40% relative to no skill. Task success can also remain unchanged while execution savings decline. These effects depend on which environment-specific details become outdated and the agent's ability to compensate using current observations. We introduce selective maintenance, which replays checks from successful executions without additional model calls. It verifies whether observed differences conflict with skill state, repairs affected content, and validates updates, rebuilding when local repair is insufficient. No description of the change is supplied. Relative to reusing stale state, maintenance improves task accuracy by up to 67pp and reduces execution steps by up to 37%. These results suggest that preserving a skill's inference time value as environments evolve requires selectively maintaining its state.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察环境变化后 agent 技能状态部分过时导致的复用失效，提出无需额外模型调用的选择性维护：重放成功执行中的检查、验证观测与状态的冲突、局部修复并校验，不足时重建。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「内部状态与当前观测冲突检测—局部修复—必要时重建」的流程，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的有效性校验、陈旧表示更新与何时放弃重算提供参照，可供核查。
